Take a shelter dog out for the day.

Hike, grab a pup cup, or host a sleepover with an adoptable dog, or spend time with shelter cats. It's free, it helps animals get adopted, and every listing is checked monthly.

The nationwide database of shelter day-out programs, updated monthly.

2,172 shelters listed nationwide, including 296 with day-out or cat programs in 47 states and Washington, DC. We search every state each month and add new programs as shelters launch them. Know a shelter we're missing?

How it works

1. Find a programSearch by city or state. 166 programs listed here are open to the public.
2. Sign up with the shelterEach listing links to the shelter's own sign-up page, rules and hours. Shelters make the match.
3. Enjoy the dayTake the dog for a hike, a coffee or a nap on your couch. The photos you share help them get adopted.

Questions people ask

Can I rent a dog for the day?

Not from a business, but you can do something better: many animal shelters let you borrow an adoptable dog for free for a few hours, a full day or a sleepover. Programs go by names like Doggy Day Out, Dog for a Day, Field Trips and Daycations.

How much does it cost to take a shelter dog out for the day?

Almost always nothing. Shelters run these programs to give dogs a break from the kennel and help them get adopted, and most send you off with a leash, an Adopt Me vest and treats.

Do I have to adopt the dog?

No. There is no commitment. If you fall in love, you can ask the shelter about adopting, but most people simply bring the dog back at the end of the outing.

Who can take a shelter dog out?

Most programs require you to be 18 or older with a photo ID and a signed waiver. Some are open to anyone who walks in; others are for trained volunteers or require booking ahead. Each listing says which.

Can I have a sleepover with a shelter dog?

Yes, many shelters offer overnights, weekend sleepovers or multi-day staycations. See shelter dog sleepovers near you.

Is there a dog day out program near me?

Search the directory above by city or state, or browse by city. We list programs in all 50 states and check them every month. If your shelter doesn't run one yet, you can still send a request.

ShelterDayOut is a free directory. We don't run outings or handle bookings; each shelter sets its own rules. Listings are checked monthly, but details change, so confirm with the shelter before you go.
